what: No reference says how to compute the per-core CB budget at runtime. The implementer replaced get_max_worker_l1_unreserved_size() with total_bytes_per_bank - total_bytes_allocated_per_bank, which ignores L1 fragmentation: a freed L1 tensor above a live one leaves a hole, the CB region must end at the LOWEST allocated block, and a solve that fills the budget throws program.cpp "circular buffers ... clash with L1 buffers". Python has no binding for device->lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address(); the only route is min(int(b["address"]) for b in ttnn.get_memory_view(device, L1).block_table if b["allocated"]=="yes").
suggest: Add a runtime-budget recipe to l1-footprint-discipline.md (or bind lowest_occupied_compute_l1_address in ttnn and point to it): budget = lowest allocated L1 offset (block_table) - reserve, never bank - allocated bytes.

what: In graded runs the L1 capture turns a PASSING expected-error test (op correctly raises ValueError before allocating, e.g. test_translated.py::test_matmul_same_shape_but_invalid) into a failure with peak_total=0. verify_supported then reports it as supported_fail/other, a loud category the verifier cannot clean without hacking the op or dishonest EXCLUSIONS.
suggest: In capture_for_item, skip (do not raise) when peak_total == 0 and the graded op window never completed a dispatch (or the test body exercised pytest.raises / expect_error).
